subject: Marketplace procurement path & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Shah <samir@lumen.ai>, procurement@lumen.ai
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace procurement path & next steps

Hi Samir — great to chat today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Objective: Get clarity on procurement path so we can surface the correct commercial option (AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace listing vs direct PO/invoice).
- LumenAI signals: interested in AWS Marketplace, prefers consolidated billing across business units.
- Action items for LumenAI: Confirm procurement contact and whether a PO or card will be used for initial evaluation (pilot).
- Action items for Redwood: Share AWS marketplace instruction playbook and a short notes doc outlining purchase order flow vs card payment.

I've attached the Redwood AWS Marketplace Playbook and a blank procurement form for you to share internally. Can you confirm who on your procurement team should receive the form and whether you expect to purchase via AWS Marketplace SaaS contracts or via a direct PO to Redwood?

If helpful, Marissa (cc'd) will lead procurement/contracting once you confirm the path. Proposed follow-up: 30-minute call next week to finalize (I'm flexible Wed/Thu).

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.inference
https://redwood.inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@lumen.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@lumen.ai
Date: 2026-10-26T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path & next steps

Thanks Camila — appreciate the recap. A few answers from our side: 

- Procurement contact: procurement@lumen.ai (cc'd here) — primary contact is Priya N.
- Preferred initial payment: We typically pilot on a card for low-dollar POCs, but any production purchase will go through PO and centralized SSO billing. For the pilot, we can start with a card and then convert to PO for the reserved capacity purchase.
- Marketplace interest: We prefer AWS Marketplace for billing consolidation; however, we'll consider direct PO if Marketplace listing doesn't support the reserved capacity SKUs we need.

I've attached a blank procurement intake form (procurement@lumen.ai internal template) for your contracting team to review. Let's schedule the 30-minute follow-up next Wed (Nov 4) at 10am PT if that works for you and Marissa.

Best,
Samir
VP, Platform Engineering
LumenAI

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Shah <samir@lumen.ai>, procurement@lumen.ai
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path & next steps

Thanks Samir — confirming Nov 4 at 10am PT works for us. Quick notes ahead of the call so we can be efficient: 

- Marissa will have the master agreement and typical AWS Marketplace listing terms on-hand and can speak to the differences in SLOs and billing cadence between a Marketplace subscription vs a direct Reserved Capacity contract.
- Ben (cc'd in future thread) will advise on pricing bands for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go.
- For the call: we want to confirm (1) pilot ordering vehicle (card vs small PO), (2) target SKU for reserved capacity (so we can check marketplace SKU availability), (3) timeline to move pilot to PO/commit.

Attached: Redwood_AWS_Marketplace_Playbook.pdf (again) and a one-page checklist of items procurement typically needs. If procurement has a preferred intake (e.g., vendor questionnaire link), please send it prior to the call.

See you on Nov 4 — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Priya N. <procurement@lumen.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Samir Shah <samir@lumen.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path & next steps

Hi Camila — apologies for the delay, been out on travel. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 

1) For a pilot under $5k, we can use a corporate card (Finance will approve). For anything >$5k we'll need a PO.
2) For production reserved capacity we will go with a PO and require Redwood to accept our standard vendor terms or sign a short addendum. We can share our PO template and vendor questionnaire.
3) AWS Marketplace is preferable, but we need to confirm whether Marketplace supports the SKU/contract structure for reserved capacity. If not, we'll do a direct PO.

I've attached our procurement intake and vendor questionnaire. Please send your master agreement and any marketplace terms we should review.

Thanks,
Priya
Procurement Manager, LumenAI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Priya N. <procurement@lumen.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Samir Shah <samir@lumen.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path & next steps

Hi Priya — thanks for the details and the intake materials. Attaching our redlined master agreement and a short notes doc that maps the two procurement paths (AWS Marketplace vs direct PO) with expected timelines and contact points. Key points here: 

- For pilots under $5k: card is fastest. We'll invoice through marketplace or directly depending on SKU availability.
- For reserved capacity / committed contracts: PO & vendor terms accepted. We can either (a) list reserved SKUs on AWS Marketplace and run the purchase through the marketplace subscription flow (may add 7–10 business days for listing verification), or (b) process a direct PO to Redwood and execute our MA (faster for large committed deals).
- Next steps I propose: (1) Camila to confirm pilot order vehicle by replying to this thread; (2) Priya to send preferred PO template if you want us to pre-populate it; (3) Ben will provide the reserved-capacity pricing bands once we have target SKUs.

Docs attached: redwood_master_agreement_v2_redlines.docx, Redwood_AWS_Marketplace_Playbook.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
